Mr. ABM Nurul Islam with Mr. Md. Nawasher Ali Mollah, Advocates ----- For the Petitioner. 
Mr. Miah Abdul Gafur, Advocate ----- For the Opposite Parties 3 and 4.
parties:
Moyezuddin Mondal ----- Petitioner.
Vs.
Bena Rani Das & others ----- Opposite Parties.
full_judgment:
The plaintiff-petitioner instituted a suit being Title Suit No. 42 of 1988 in the Court of the Subordinate Judge, Rajbari for specific performance of a contract for sale of the schedule property against the defendants opposite parties on the allegations, inter alia that the defendant-opposite party No. 1 was the owner of the suit property on the basis of a transfer deed dated 2.4.1937. Her name was mutated in the khatians and she used to pay taxes in her name and also lives in the suit-holding along with two monthly tenants; that her husband died and she became a widow with her 2 daughters who however being married became inhabitants of India. Hence she tried to live elsewhere with her other relations inside the country after selling out the suit-property. The plaintiff-petitioner being her closest neighbour wanted to purchase the same and a deed of agreement (bainanama) for sale between the plaintiff and defendant No. 1 was accordingly executed on 25.2.1987 fixing the consideration of the suit-property at Tk. 2 lac out of which Tk. 1 lac 15 thousand was paid to the defendant No. 1 on the day of agreement on condition that after obtaining Income Tax clearance certificate defendant No. 1 would execute and register the necessary sale deed in favour of the plaintiff. The plaintiff thereafter with the permission of the defendant No. 1 started to reside in the disputed holding and the said two tenants in the holding used to pay their house rents to him; that the plaintiff-petitioner requested the defendant No. 1 several times and lastly on 26.6.88 to execute and register the necessary sale-deed but that having been refused, the plaintiff petitioner has been constrained to institute the present suit; defendant No. 1 since dead, during her life-time filed a written statement on 18.9.88 to contest the suit contending inter alia that she decided to sell out the property in question to defendant Nos. 2 and 3 after obtaining necessary stamps from the treasury and ultimately she had sold out the suit-property to the defendants 2 and 3 by two registered deeds dated 29.6.88 and divested all her right, title and interest in the same in their favour that the plaintiff-petitioner played a foul game with her daughter from jail custody when he managed to obtain her signatures on some blank white papers allegedly necessary for release .of her said daughter and she absolutely on good faith had signed the same; it was further alleged that her tenants have or had never paid rents to the plaintiff petitioner as claimed; that the deed of agreement is false, fabricated and a back dated one and, in fact, no such deed of agreement has been executed between the defendant No. 1 and the plaintiff-petitioner; that the co-defendant Nos. 2 and 3 also filed a separate joint written statement on 28.12.88 contending, inter alia, that they are the real purchasers of the suit property by two different kabalas dated 29.6.88 for a valuable consideration from the defendant No. 1 and they are in possession of the suit property but the tenants being in collusion with the plaintiff are not paying any rent to them and that the alleged deed of agreement and the rent receipts are false and back dated. The suit however proceeded and the plaintiff-petitioner filed two applications on 25.2.89, one for amendment of the plaint and another for reception of some documents in evidence filed by a firisti. These applications came up for hearing on 26.3.89 before the learned Subordinate Judge, Rajbari and on that day the plaintiff also filed another application for substitution of the legal heirs of defendant No. 1 on her death and for amendment of the plaint accordingly. All these applications were heard together. And after hearing both the sides at length, the learned Subordinate Judge was pleased to allow the prayer for substitution of the legal heirs of the deceased defendant No. 1 and admit some documents in that connection, but rejected the prayer for reception of the documents of the plaintiff- petitioners as filed by a firisti and also refused the prayer for amendment of the plaint by his judgment and order dated 16.3.89. Being aggrieved by the said order so far as it relates to the rejection of the plaintiffs prayer for reception of the concerned documents and for amendment of the plaint, the plaintiff-petitioner moved a revisional application and obtained the present rule. 

 If, we now read these two rules together, we find that before the aforesaid amendment according to rule 14, the plaintiff was required to produce the documents upon which he would institute the suit. At the same time he was to deliver a copy thereof to be filed along with the plaint. Now, this provision has been deleted and according to the present amendment of rule 14 Order VII, the plaintiff shall have to produce the documents in his possession or power which he wants to rely upon as evidence in support of his claim, when the plaint is presented in court and those have to be delivered and filed along with the plaint. In the instant case at the time of institution of the suit, the plaintiff petitioner filed some of his documents to be relied upon in support of his claim which were in his possession, but he could not file some other documents as they were temporarily missing but on their recovery sometime after he filed the same by a firisti with an application explaining the delay and the exceptional circumstances and seeking leave of the Court for their acceptance. Rule 18 of Order VII clearly speaks of reception of the documents filed at a later stage with leave of the Court which leave should be granted in exceptional circumstances. In the instant case the suit was instituted on 16.8.88 and the missing documents on their recovery were filed by a firisti on 25.2.89 i.e. after a delay of about 6 months and a few days which in our view cannot be called to be an inordinate delay in the facts and circumstances of the case. It appears from the first paragraph of the plaint, a copy of which has been shown to us that there is some reference relating to the said documents by the plaintiff and from the certified copy of the firisti we find that in all 13 documents in original along with 13 photo copies of the same relating to payment of municipal taxes, land taxes, etc. paid by the defendant No. 1 Nihar Bala and also relating to SA khatian and RS khatian in respect of the suit holding were submitted in court for acceptance. It has not been found by the Subordinate Judge that those documents are suspicious or not genuine but still he has refused to admit them in evidence only by a casual reference to the amendment of 1983 of the Code of Civil Procedure without any specification or discussion of the same which shows that he has passed the impugned order of rejection without proper application of his judicial mind and as such the same cannot be sustained in law and is liable to be set aside Mr. ABM Nurul Islam, the learned Advocate for the petitioner, in support of his contention has relied on a decision in the case of Fazal Elahi @ Sk. Fazal Elahi Vs. Shah Alam reported in 25 DLR 62 in which it has been observed that 

 "8. that at the time of accepting the deed of agreement by the defendant No. 1 with the plaintiff, the original document dated 2.4.1937 having been lost during war of liberation, she handed over to them a registered copy of the same dated 13.9.1976 along with Rent Receipts, Municipal Taxes khatians and other papers. That the plaintiff never be fooled the defendant No. 1 and never obtained her signature in a blank stamp-paper in the name of her daughter in jail and she has signed the said agreement out of her free will."
